chapterNote: A Hallelujah mosaic — a psalm built almost entirely from other Scriptures, sung by the temple's servants standing in the courts. Praise the LORD, for He is good, and make music to His name, for it is pleasant; He chose Jacob, Israel as His treasured possession. Then the reasons, in order: He is over all gods; He does whatever He pleases in heaven and earth and sea and deeps; He raises the clouds, makes lightning for the rain, brings the wind from His storehouses; He struck Egypt's firstborn, sent signs against Pharaoh, struck great nations and mighty kings — Sihon, Og, all the kingdoms of Canaan — and gave their land to Israel. His name endures forever; He will vindicate His people. And then, lifted almost straight from Psalm 115, the satire of the idols: silver and gold, mouths that do not speak, eyes, ears — and, this psalm's own addition, no breath — and those who make them become like them. The ending is Psalm 115's threefold call turned into a fourfold blessing — house of Israel, house of Aaron, house of Levi, you who fear the LORD — and the LORD Himself blessed out of Zion, He who dwells in Jerusalem, and a closing Hallelujah.

1.text: Praise the LORD! Praise the name of the LORD; give praise, you servants of the LORD,
1.amp: Praise [halal] ye the LORD [Yah]. Praise ye the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH]; praise Him, O ye servants [ebed] of the LORD.
1.notes: halelu-Yah, halelu et-shem YHWH, halelu abde YHWH — praise Yah, praise the name of the LORD, praise, you servants of the LORD — (H1984, H3050, H8034, H3068, H5650): three halal's — Psalm 113:1's opening reversed in order. The abde YHWH are the temple staff of verse 2, the Levites on duty.

2.text: you who stand on duty in the house of the LORD, in the courts of our God's house.
2.amp: Ye that stand [amad] in the house [bayith] of the LORD [YHWH], in the courts [chatser] of the house of our God [Elohim].
2.notes: she-omedim be-bet YHWH (H5975, H1004, H3068): those STANDING — on duty — in the LORD's house — be-chatsrot bet Elohenu (H2691, H430): in the courts. Psalm 134:1's night-watch servants, here without the time-marker, told to lead the praise.

3.text: Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good; make music to His name, for it is pleasant.
3.amp: Praise [halal] the LORD [Yah]; for the LORD [YHWH] is good [tov]: sing praises [zamar] unto His name [shem]; for it is pleasant [naim — delightful].
3.notes: halelu-Yah ki-tov YHWH (H1984, H3050, H2896, H3068): praise, for He is GOOD — the confession of Psalm 100:5 and the opening line of Psalms 106, 107, 118 and 136 — zammeru li-shmo ki naim (H2167, H8034, H5273): make music to the Name, for it is pleasant — naim, the delight-word of Psalm 133:1 and 147:1. Praise is enjoyable — the psalm says so, and Psalm 147:1 says it twice.

4.text: For the LORD has chosen Jacob for Himself — Israel, as His own treasured possession.
4.amp: For the LORD [Yah] has chosen [bachar] Jacob [Yaaqob] unto Himself, and Israel [Yisrael] for His peculiar treasure [segullah — personal treasure, prized possession].
4.notes: ki-Yaaqob bachar lo Yah (H3290, H977, H3050): Jacob CHOSEN — Yisrael li-segullato (H3478, H5459): as His segullah, the king's private treasure-chest as opposed to the public purse (cf. Exodus 19:5; 1 Chronicles 29:3). Election as being kept in the King's own strongbox; 1 Peter 2:9 hands the word to the church.

5.text: For I myself know that the LORD is great, and that our Lord is over all gods.
5.amp: For I know [yada] that the LORD [YHWH] is great [gadol], and that our Lord [Adon] is above all gods [elohim].
5.notes: ki ani yadati ki-gadol YHWH (H3045, H1419, H3068): I KNOW — personal knowledge in a congregational psalm — va-Adonenu mi-kol-elohim (H113, H430): our Lord above all gods, Exodus 18:11's confession, Jethro's after the exodus. The 'gods' will be inspected in verses 15-18.

6.text: Whatever the LORD pleases, He does — in heaven and on earth, in the seas and in all the deeps.
6.amp: Whatsoever the LORD [YHWH] pleased [chaphets], that did [asah] He in heaven [shamayim], and in earth [eretz], in the seas [yam], and all deep places [tehom].
6.notes: kol asher-chaphets YHWH asah (H2654, H3068, H6213): Psalm 115:3's sovereignty clause, extended: ba-shamayim u-ba-aretz, ba-yammim ve-khol-tehomot (H8064, H776, H3220, H8415) — four realms, top to bottom, sky to abyss. There is no jurisdiction where His pleasure does not run.

7.text: He brings the clouds up from the ends of the earth; He makes lightning for the rain; He brings the wind out of His storehouses.
7.amp: He causes the vapours [nasi — rising mists, clouds] to ascend [alah] from the ends [qatseh] of the earth [eretz]; He makes [asah] lightnings [baraq] for the rain [matar]; He brings [yatsa] the wind [ruach] out of His treasuries [otsar — storehouses].
7.notes: maaleh nesiim mi-qtseh ha-aretz (H5927, H5387, H7097, H776): the nesiim — spelled like nasi, 'prince' (both from nasa, to lift; Strong's files them together, the lexicons split them), here the lifted vapors — lifted from the earth's edge; beraqim la-matar asah (H1300, H4306, H6213): lightning made FOR the rain, the flash that brings the shower; motse-ruach me-otsrotav (H3318, H7307, H214): wind from His storehouses. Jeremiah 10:13 (repeated at 51:16) has the same three clauses nearly word for word; weather as God's logistics.

8.text: He struck down the firstborn of Egypt, of man and beast alike.
8.amp: Who smote [nakah] the firstborn [bekor] of Egypt [Mitsrayim], both of man ['from man unto beast', adam, the KJV margin] and beast [behemah].
8.notes: she-hikkah bekhore Mitsrayim (H5221, H1060, H4714): the tenth plague — me-adam ad-behemah (H120, H929): the margin's 'from man to beast', Exodus 12:12's scope. From weather to history: the same hand.

9.text: He sent signs and wonders into your midst, O Egypt — against Pharaoh and against all his servants.
9.amp: Who sent [shalach] tokens [ot — signs] and wonders [mopheth] into the midst [tavek] of you, O Egypt [Mitsrayim], upon Pharaoh [Paroh], and upon all his servants [ebed].
9.notes: shalach otot u-mophetim be-tokhekhi Mitsrayim (H7971, H226, H4159, H8432, H4714): signs and wonders SENT into Egypt's midst — Deuteronomy's standard pair for the plagues — be-Pharoh u-be-khol-abadav (H6547, H5650): on Pharaoh and all his servants. The psalm addresses Egypt directly, as if she were in the congregation.

10.text: He struck down many nations and slew mighty kings —
10.amp: Who smote [nakah] great [rav — many] nations [goy], and slew [harag] mighty [atsum — numerous, strong] kings [melek];
10.notes: she-hikkah goyim rabbim (H5221, H1471, H7227): many nations struck — ve-harag melakhim atsumim (H2026, H4428, H6099): and mighty kings slain. Psalm 136:17-18's couplet, the Transjordan campaign about to be itemized.

11.text: Sihon the king of the Amorites, and Og the king of Bashan, and every kingdom of Canaan —
11.amp: Sihon [Sichon] king [melek] of the Amorites [Emori], and Og [Og] king of Bashan [Bashan], and all the kingdoms [mamlakah] of Canaan [Kenaan]:
11.notes: le-Sichon melekh ha-Emori u-le-Og melekh ha-Bashan (H5511, H4428, H567, H5747, H1316): the two Transjordan kings of Numbers 21, named as in Psalm 136:19-20 — u-le-khol mamlekhot Kenaan (H4467, H3667): and all Canaan's kingdoms, Joshua's thirty-one. The conquest in one verse.

12.text: and He gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel His people.
12.amp: And gave [natan] their land [eretz] for an heritage [nachalah — inheritance], an heritage unto Israel [Yisrael] His people [am].
12.notes: ve-natan artsam nachalah (H5414, H776, H5159): their land given as nachalah — nachalah le-Yisrael ammo (H3478, H5971): the word repeated, inheritance to Israel His people. Psalm 136:21-22, with 'His people' where 136 had 'His servant'.

13.text: O LORD, Your name endures forever; Your memorial, O LORD, from generation to generation.
13.amp: Your name [shem], O LORD [YHWH], endures for ever [olam]; and Your memorial [zeker — the name by which You are remembered], O LORD, throughout all generations ['to generation and generation', dor va-dor, the KJV margin].
13.notes: YHWH shimkha le-olam (H3068, H8034, H5769): Your Name forever — YHWH zikhrekha le-dor va-dor (H2143, H1755): Your zeker, Your memorial-name, generation to generation — Exodus 3:15's own words: 'this is My name forever, and this is My memorial to all generations'. The psalm quotes the burning bush.

14.text: For the LORD will vindicate His people, and He will have compassion on His servants.
14.amp: For the LORD [YHWH] will judge [din — vindicate, plead the cause of] His people [am], and He will repent [nacham — relent, have compassion] Himself concerning His servants [ebed].
14.notes: ki-yadin YHWH ammo (H1777, H3068, H5971): din here is to judge FOR — to vindicate, to take up the case of — ve-al-abadav yitnecham (H5650, H5162): and concerning His servants He will relent, have compassion. the first half of Deuteronomy 32:36 verbatim, from the Song of Moses: the psalm keeps quoting.

15.text: The nations' idols are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
15.amp: The idols [atsab — fashioned images] of the heathen [goy] are silver [keseph] and gold [zahab], the work [maaseh] of men's [adam] hands [yad].
15.notes: atsabbe ha-goyim keseph ve-zahab (H6091, H1471, H3701, H2091): Psalm 115:4-8 begins to be quoted — maaseh yede adam (H4639, H3027, H120): human handiwork. After ten verses (5-14) of what the LORD does, the psalm inspects what the rivals are: manufactured.

16.text: Mouths they have, but they do not speak; eyes they have, but they do not see;
16.amp: They have mouths [peh], but they speak [dabar] not; eyes [ayin] have they, but they see [raah] not;
16.notes: peh-lahem ve-lo yedabberu (H6310, H1696), enayim lahem ve-lo yiru (H5869, H7200): Psalm 115:5, a mouth to them and they do not speak, eyes to them and they do not see — the corpse-inventory: organs without functions.

17.text: they have ears, but do not hear; indeed, there is no breath at all in their mouths.
17.amp: They have ears [ozen], but they hear [azan] not; neither is there [yesh] any breath [ruach] in their mouths [peh].
17.notes: oznayim lahem ve-lo yaazinu (H241, H238): ears that do not give ear — the verb is the ear's own — aph en-yesh-ruach be-phihem (H3426, H7307, H6310): and there is NO breath in their mouths — the line Psalm 115 did not have: the idols do not breathe, while the LORD of Psalm 104:30 sends His ruach and things are created.

18.text: Those who make them become like them — so does everyone who trusts in them.
18.amp: They that make [asah] them are like unto them: so is every one that trusts [batach] in them.
18.notes: kemohem yihyu osehem (H6213): the makers become like the made — kol asher-boteach bahem (H982): and everyone trusting in them. Psalm 115:8 exactly: the law that worship is formative, and dead gods make dead worshipers.

19.text: You house of Israel, bless the LORD! You house of Aaron, bless the LORD!
19.amp: Bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH], O house [bayith] of Israel [Yisrael]: bless the LORD, O house of Aaron [Aharon]:
19.notes: bet Yisrael barakhu et-YHWH (H1004, H3478, H1288, H3068), bet Aharon barakhu et-YHWH (H175): Psalm 115:9-10's two houses, now told to BLESS rather than trust — the response to the idols is doxology.

20.text: House of Levi, you too, bless the LORD! You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!
20.amp: Bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH], O house [bayith] of Levi [Levi]: ye that fear [yare] the LORD, bless the LORD.
20.notes: bet ha-Levi barakhu et-YHWH (H1004, H3878, H1288): a fourth ring Psalm 115 did not have — the house of Levi, the temple servants of verse 2 — yire YHWH barakhu et-YHWH (H3373): and the God-fearers, the open category. Four summonses to bless, matching the four realms of verse 6.

21.text: Blessed be the LORD out of Zion, He who dwells in Jerusalem! Praise the LORD!
21.amp: Blessed [barak] be the LORD [YHWH] out of Zion [Tsiyyon], which dwells [shakan] at Jerusalem [Yerushalaim]. Praise [halal] ye the LORD [Yah].
21.notes: barukh YHWH mi-Tsiyyon (H1288, H3068, H6726): blessed from Zion, Psalm 134:3's direction reversed — the blessing that came down from Zion now goes back up from it — shokhen Yerushalaim (H7931, H3389): the One who TABERNACLES in Jerusalem, the shekinah-verb. halelu-Yah (H1984, H3050): the mosaic closes with the word it opened with.
